Dish (local name): Khambir + Gur-gur cha (butter tea); or Kholak (ngamphe/tsampa mixed into butter tea)
English name: Thick local wheat bread with salty butter tea; or roasted-barley-flour dough made with the tea
Ingredients: Khambir: whole-wheat flour, water, yeast/sourdough, salt. Butter tea: brick or black tea, water, salt, butter, milk. Kholak: roasted barley flour (ngamphe), butter tea
Cooking method (key steps, vessel, time): Khambir dough rested and baked or griddled into a thick round. Tea boiled long, then churned with butter and salt in a tall wooden churn (or blender) until frothy. Kholak: tea poured onto barley flour and kneaded by hand - no cooking.
Unique fact [sources]: Butter tea (gur-gur cha) is salty, not sweet: tea churned with butter and salt. Rice was once a luxury in Ladakh; subsidised rice from the plains is now a staple, partly displacing local barley (S69; debated in S70). Leh became one of 8 Ladakh districts in 2026. [S68; S69; S70; S72; S73]
Notes / alternatives: Only one countable source (S68, academic); S71 is a travel operator (pointer only). Needs a second tier A-C source or a local reviewer. Kholak and butter tea are described as quick, low-fuel breakfasts by IJTK (S68). Traditional pattern - many modern Leh homes also eat bread, eggs or paratha.

English name: Rice and lentils with seasonal vegetables; or skyu, thumb-pressed wheat pasta in vegetable/meat stew

Dish (local name): Morning rice meal: Rice + boiled seasonal greens + Tathu (chilli chutney)
English name: Rice with simply boiled greens and a fresh chilli chutney - many Naga homes eat a full rice meal in the morning
Ingredients: Rice; mustard leaves or other greens; chutney of king chilli or other chilli, tomato, salt (sometimes fermented soybean or dried fish)
Cooking method (key steps, vessel, time): Rice boiled; greens boiled with salt (little or no oil); chilli and tomato roasted or pounded with salt in a mortar.
Unique fact [sources]: Naga kitchens preserve meat by smoking it on racks above the hearth for days to weeks. The Naga King Chilli (Raja Mircha) got a GI tag in 2008 and measures about 1,000,000 Scoville units - over 100x a jalapeno. [S76; S77; S80; S78]
Notes / alternatives: 'Rice up to twice a day' (Angami) comes from secondary pages - confirm with a local reviewer before saying 'breakfast is a full rice meal' on screen.
